# SQRL-1

SQRL-1 is firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, built on [Felucca](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca). It replaces the
FM-1's screens with a shell of its own, and every instrument in it is a nut: a SOUND that makes the
tone, or a NOTE engine that decides which notes to play. You play a pair of them, one of each.

<img src="img/flow.svg" alt="Keys to the NOTE engine to the SOUND, through the part's own effects, the shared effects, and out">

The tables, ranges, factory sounds and screens on every page are generated from the firmware, so they match the
build they ship with.

## SOUND nuts

A SOUND is a synthesis engine with its own pages and factory sounds. SQRL-1 has eight, one on each of the wheel's
white keys. The other engines Felucca and databurn wrote are [on the sidelines](sidelines.md): in the source, each
back with a build flag, and a sound saved on one of them plays on its nearest of the eight.

| | Nut | What it does | Reach it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <img src="img/glyph_fm6.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [FM6](sound/fm6.md) | plays six-operator FM | white key C4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_lizard.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [LIZARD](sound/lizard.md) | draw the wave | white key D4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_drums.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [DRUMS](sound/drums.md) | plays drum kits | white key F4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_shock.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [SHOCK](sound/shock.md) | steepens a sine into brass | white key E4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_analog.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [ANALOG](sound/analog.md) | filters two oscillators | white key A4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_phase.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [PHASE](sound/phase.md) | bends a cosine, CZ style | white key B4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_phys.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [PHYS](sound/phys.md) | rings bars and strings | white key C5 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_mouth.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [MOUTH](sound/mouth.md) | sings words, SAM style | white key G4 in the wheel |

## NOTE nuts

A NOTE engine sits between the keys and the SOUND. KEYS passes your playing through as it is; the others turn a
key into a chord, a strum or a walk around the Tonnetz, answer it in canon, or grow a melody by themselves.

| | Nut | What it does | Reach it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <img src="img/glyph_keys.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [KEYS](note/keys.md) | you play | black key C#4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_chord.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [CHORD](note/chord.md) | plays a chord per key | black key D#4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_alive.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [ALIVE](note/alive.md) | grows notes from an automaton | the slot picker |
| <img src="img/glyph_tonnetz.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [TONNETZ](note/tonnetz.md) | walks a triad round the Tonnetz | black key G#4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_enigma.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [ENIGMA](note/enigma.md) | loops a phrase and mutates it | the slot picker |
| <img src="img/glyph_harp.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [HARP](note/harp.md) | strums a chord on the keys | the slot picker |
| <img src="img/glyph_rudiment.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [RUDIMENT](note/rudiment.md) | builds a beat on the keys | black key A#4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_lines.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [LINES](note/lines.md) | plays a line in lanes | black key F#4 in the wheel |
| <img src="img/glyph_s-h.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [S+H](note/s-h.md) | samples a source into the scale | the slot picker |
| <img src="img/glyph_canon.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [CANON](note/canon.md) | answers what you play | the slot picker |
| <img src="img/glyph_acid.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> | [ACID](note/acid.md) | plays a 303 line | the slot picker |

## Reading this manual

Install it with [Getting started](start.md), then read [The shell](shell.md) and
[The wheel](wheel.md): the same few gestures work in every nut. Each nut's page starts with what you play (its keys
and the four knobs on its MAIN page), then shows its deeper pages as the FM-1's screen draws them.

Knob tables give each knob's label, its range and the value it starts at when you first open the nut. Knobs are
numbered left to right, and the coloured dot matches the dot on the screen.
